safety_observation.name: safety_observation
safety_observation.description: A safety observation refers to any recorded note or report about workplace conditions, behaviors, or practices that may impact health and safety. These observations are typically made by workers, supervisors, or safety personnel during routine checks or daily activities to identify both safe and unsafe practices. They help in proactively identifying trends and preventing incidents.
examples: Observed worker wearing proper PPE in the welding area.
Noted that emergency exits were clear during shift change.
Identified safe lifting practices being followed in warehouse.
Observed forklift operator using seatbelt as required.
Noted that spill kits were fully stocked and accessible.

near_miss.name: near_miss
near_miss.description: A near miss is an unplanned event that did not result in injury, illness, or damage but had the potential to do so. In HSE, near misses are reported to identify hazards and prevent future incidents by addressing underlying causes before harm occurs.
examples: A falling tool narrowly missed a worker's foot but caused no injury.
Forklift reversed into a walkway but stopped before hitting anyone.
Chemical container slipped but was caught before spilling.
Worker tripped over hose but regained balance and was not hurt.
Overhead load swung unexpectedly but did not strike any personnel.

incident.name: incident
incident.description: An incident is any unplanned event that results in or could have resulted in injury, illness, property damage, or environmental harm. In HSE, incidents are formally reported and investigated to determine root causes and prevent recurrence.
examples: Worker sustained a laceration while using a box cutter.
Oil spill occurred during equipment maintenance.
Employee slipped on wet floor and sprained ankle.
Fire alarm triggered due to electrical short circuit.
Forklift collided with storage rack causing minor damage.

hazard_report.name: hazard_report
hazard_report.description: A hazard report documents the identification of a potential source of harm or danger in the workplace. These reports are used to alert management and safety teams to risks that need to be assessed and controlled to prevent incidents.
examples: Reported exposed wiring near the loading dock.
Identified unguarded machinery in production area.
Noted chemical storage area lacking proper signage.
Reported loose handrail on main staircase.
Observed blocked fire extinguisher access.

environmental_observation.name: environmental_observation
environmental_observation.description: An environmental observation records any condition or event that may impact the environment, such as pollution, waste, or wildlife disturbances. In HSE, these observations help monitor compliance with environmental regulations and identify areas for improvement.
examples: Observed oil sheen on surface water near outfall.
Noted excessive dust emissions from conveyor belt.
Reported improper disposal of chemical containers.
Identified wildlife nesting near storage tanks.
Observed waste bins overflowing in outdoor area.

quality_issue.name: quality_issue
quality_issue.description: A quality issue refers to any observation or report of a product, process, or service not meeting established standards or specifications. In HSE, quality issues can relate to defective equipment, substandard materials, or process deviations that may also pose safety or environmental risks.
examples: Found welds not meeting inspection criteria on pressure vessel.
Reported batch of safety gloves with torn seams.
Identified mislabeled chemical drums in storage.
Noted paint finish defects on equipment panels.
Observed incorrect assembly of machine guards.

maintenance_request.name: maintenance_request
maintenance_request.description: A maintenance request is a formal notification to repair, replace, or service equipment, infrastructure, or safety systems. In HSE, timely maintenance requests help prevent equipment failures, unsafe conditions, and ensure compliance with safety standards.
examples: Requested repair of leaking hydraulic hose on forklift.
Submitted work order for malfunctioning emergency lighting.
Reported broken guardrail on mezzanine platform.
Requested servicing of air quality monitoring system.
Notified maintenance of faulty fire alarm panel.

unsafe_condition.name: unsafe_condition
unsafe_condition.description: An unsafe condition is any physical state or environmental factor in the workplace that could lead to injury, illness, or property damage. Reporting unsafe conditions is critical in HSE to eliminate hazards before they result in incidents.
examples: Wet floor in corridor without warning signs.
Unsecured ladder left in walkway.
Damaged electrical outlet near water source.
Poor lighting in stairwell area.
Obstructed emergency exit door.

unsafe_act.name: unsafe_act
unsafe_act.description: An unsafe act is any behavior or action by a person that increases the risk of an accident or injury. In HSE, these acts are observed and reported to correct unsafe behaviors and reinforce safe work practices.
examples: Worker bypassed machine guard during operation.
Employee climbed shelving to reach high item.
Operator used mobile phone while driving forklift.
Technician failed to lock out equipment before maintenance.
Worker did not wear required eye protection in lab.

month.name: month
month.description: In HSE analytics, 'month' refers to a calendar period of approximately 30 days used for tracking, reporting, and analyzing safety and environmental data. Monthly intervals are commonly used to identify trends, monitor compliance, and assess the frequency of incidents, near misses, or hazards over time. Observations and reports are often grouped by month to facilitate regular reviews and targeted interventions.
examples: Three near misses were reported in the month of April.
Monthly safety inspections identified two new hazards.
No lost time injuries occurred last month.
Environmental spill incidents increased this month compared to the previous month.
Monthly review showed improved PPE compliance.

quarter.name: quarter
quarter.description: In the HSE context, 'quarter' denotes a three-month period used for summarizing and comparing safety, health, and environmental performance. Quarterly analysis helps organizations identify patterns, evaluate the effectiveness of interventions, and comply with regulatory or internal reporting requirements. Events, incidents, and observations are often aggregated by quarter for management review and strategic planning.
examples: There were five recordable injuries in the second quarter.
Quarterly environmental audits were completed on schedule.
Near miss reports increased in Q3 compared to Q2.
Quarterly review highlighted a reduction in unsafe conditions.
Quarterly safety meetings addressed recurring hazards.

year.name: year
year.description: In HSE analytics, 'year' refers to a twelve-month period used for comprehensive tracking and evaluation of safety, health, and environmental performance. Annual data aggregation supports long-term trend analysis, regulatory compliance, and strategic decision-making. Yearly summaries often include total incidents, major events, and progress toward safety goals.
examples: The site recorded zero fatalities this year.
Annual safety training was completed by all employees.
Yearly incident rate decreased compared to last year.
Environmental compliance was maintained throughout the year.
Year-end review identified key areas for safety improvement.

production.name: production
production.description: In HSE, the production department refers to areas and teams directly involved in manufacturing, processing, or assembling products. Observations here often relate to machine operation, line safety, process hazards, and worker behaviors on the shop floor. Typical events include equipment malfunctions, unsafe practices, or process deviations impacting safety or environment.
examples: Operator bypassed machine guard during shift.
Spill of coolant observed near the assembly line.
Unlabeled chemical container found in production area.
Worker not wearing ear protection in manufacturing zone.
Conveyor belt emergency stop not functioning.

maintenance.name: maintenance
maintenance.description: The maintenance department handles the upkeep, repair, and servicing of equipment, machinery, and facilities. HSE observations here often involve lockout/tagout compliance, tool safety, working at heights, and risks during repairs or inspections. Incidents may include near misses during equipment servicing or unsafe conditions in maintenance workshops.
examples: Technician did not use lockout procedure before repair.
Oil spill left unattended in maintenance workshop.
Missing guard on grinder in maintenance area.
Improper ladder use observed during HVAC servicing.
Loose tools found on top of equipment after maintenance.

quality.name: quality
quality.description: The quality department oversees product standards, inspections, and compliance with quality protocols. In HSE, this area often intersects with safe sampling, handling of test materials, and ensuring that quality checks do not introduce hazards. Observations may include unsafe sample handling or non-compliance with inspection procedures.
examples: Sample bottles not labeled correctly in quality lab.
Inspector not wearing gloves during product testing.
Spilled reagent left on quality control bench.
Quality check area blocked by pallets.
Improper disposal of test materials observed.

logistics.name: logistics
logistics.description: The logistics department manages the movement, storage, and distribution of materials and products. HSE concerns here include vehicle safety, loading/unloading hazards, traffic management, and manual handling risks. Observations often involve forklift operations, blocked emergency exits, or unsafe stacking of goods.
examples: Forklift operated at excessive speed in loading bay.
Pallets stacked unsafely in receiving area.
Truck driver not wearing high-visibility vest.
Blocked fire exit in logistics corridor.
Manual lifting of heavy boxes without assistance.

administration.name: administration
administration.description: The administration department covers office-based staff and support functions such as HR, finance, and management. HSE observations here typically relate to office ergonomics, fire safety, slips/trips, and emergency preparedness in administrative areas. Events may include blocked evacuation routes or improper use of office equipment.
examples: Blocked emergency exit in admin office.
Loose cables causing trip hazard under desks.
Fire extinguisher missing from reception area.
Improper use of extension cords in finance office.
Unattended spill in administrative hallway.

safety.name: safety
safety.description: The safety department is responsible for implementing and monitoring health and safety policies, conducting risk assessments, and ensuring regulatory compliance. Observations here include safety audits, incident investigations, PPE compliance checks, and training activities. Events often involve identification of hazards or follow-up on corrective actions.
examples: Safety officer conducted PPE compliance inspection.
Near miss reported during safety walkthrough.
Outdated safety signage found in stairwell.
Incident investigation initiated by safety team.
Safety training session held for new employees.

engineering.name: engineering
engineering.description: The engineering department designs, modifies, and oversees technical systems, equipment, and processes. HSE observations here may involve design-related hazards, unsafe modifications, or risks during project work and commissioning. Events can include inadequate guarding on new equipment or unsafe temporary setups during installations.
examples: Temporary wiring installed without proper protection.
Engineering drawing did not specify safety barriers.
Unapproved modification to process line observed.
Commissioning team not following lockout procedures.
Missing handrails on newly installed platform.

warehouse.name: warehouse
warehouse.description: The warehouse department is responsible for storing raw materials, components, and finished goods. HSE issues here include storage safety, fire risks, manual handling, and vehicle movement within the warehouse. Observations often involve blocked aisles, unsafe stacking, or improper use of lifting equipment.
examples: Aisle blocked by pallets in warehouse.
Racking damaged and not reported.
Employee lifting heavy box without assistance.
Forklift parked in emergency exit route.
Fire extinguisher obstructed by stored goods.

operations.name: operations
operations.description: The operations department oversees the day-to-day running of plant or site activities, often coordinating between production, maintenance, and other functions. HSE observations here may cover process safety, shift handovers, emergency response, and general site management. Events can include process upsets, unsafe shift practices, or operational deviations.
examples: Process upset reported during night shift operations.
Incomplete handover between operations teams.
Operator failed to follow standard operating procedure.
Emergency drill conducted by operations staff.
Unauthorized personnel found in control room.

facility_management.name: facility_management
facility_management.description: Facility management covers the upkeep, safety, and functionality of buildings, grounds, and infrastructure. HSE observations here include building maintenance, fire safety systems, environmental controls, and general housekeeping. Events may involve faulty emergency lighting, unsafe walkways, or issues with HVAC and utilities.
examples: Emergency exit lights not working in main corridor.
Wet floor sign missing after cleaning in lobby.
Blocked access to fire hose reel in facility area.
HVAC filter replacement overdue in office wing.
Broken handrail reported on facility staircase.
